To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the one-loop anomolous dimensions of all local operators in = 4 SYM can be calculated using integrable spin chains; that the one-loop correlators in SYM can be computed from matrix elements of spin chain operators; and that the one-loop correlation function of the Konishi operator is a constant, independent of the number of points.

the Yang-Mills dilatation operator can be expressed in terms of the XXX1/ 2 chain Hamiltonian, the Yang-Mills two- and three-point functions can be expressed in matrix elements of spin chain transfer matrices and the spin chain Hamiltonian, and the Yang-Mills four-point functions can be written in terms of the Yang-Mills three-point functions.

(1) The one-loop anomalous dimension of an arbitrary gauge invariant operator can be expressed in terms of the expectation value of the spin chain Hamiltonian in a state with the operator as a spin operator, and (2) Correlation functions of gauge invariant operators can be expressed in term of expectation values of products of spin chain Hamiltonians.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relation of Yang-Mills theory in the planar limit to the theory of integrable spin systems.
the relation between Yang-Mills theory in 4 dimensions and integrable spin chain systems.
the calculation of the anomalous dimensions of gauge invariant operators of = 4 super Yang-Mills theory in the planar limit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Yang-Mills theory is a nontrivial theory.

the integrable structure of the dilatation operators of N=4 SYM is not only a useful computational tool, but that it is an essential ingredient in the construction of a consistent and predictive theory.
the dilatation operators for all the integrable sectors of = 4 SYM are exactly solvable and can be expressed in terms of integrable spin chain Hamiltonians.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Yang-Mills correlation function is given by a sum over a set of spin operators on an integrable spin chain.

the integrable spin chain description of Yang-Mills theory is very powerful in computing anomalous dimensions of single trace operators, and it is also powerful in computing correlation functions of such operators.

the one-loop dilatation operator is equivalent to an integrable spin chain, and the correlation function of a set of operators is given by a sum of matrix elements of the spin operators of the corresponding spin chain, with the operators in the set being the spin chain eigenstates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given operator, the matrix elements of spin chain operators on it are universal, i.e., they do not depend on the details of the operator under consideration.
, in the planar limit, the Yang-Mills S-matrix is a universal object that determines all the correlation functions of the theory.
the integrability of spin chains allows one to calculate the anomalous dimensions and the matrix elements of the spin operators on the same footing.
